D019-D020_h001.question: It's been a few weeks now, or maybe a month, I'm not really good with dates anymore. Ever since... well, since John passed, things just haven't been right. I try to sleep, I really do, but I wake up feeling just as tired as when I lay down, no matter how many hours I manage to get in. Sometimes, it's even worse. I'll be doing the dishes, or dusting, and all of a sudden, I'm back there, in the hospital room, seeing him… like it's happening all over again. It's just a flash, but it takes my breath away. I know he's gone, but it feels so real sometimes that I just freeze up. I don't know what's wrong with me.
D019-D020_h001.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h001.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h002.question: It's been a rough couple of weeks, doc. Sleep’s a joke. I nod off, sure, but then I'm wide awake around 2 AM, staring at the ceiling, my mind just racing. Then there are the dreams... I keep having these messed-up dreams, always about getting into some kind of accident, or losing control of the cab. I watch a lot of other drivers on the road; I see them make stupid mistakes, and I just keep imagining how that could go wrong... It’s not always exact, but the feeling of panic and being helpless is always there when I wake up in a cold sweat. It just leaves me feeling keyed up most of the day. Every little thing makes me jump, and I can't seem to shake this feeling of dread. It’s like I’m waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? My ex-wife says I’m just stressed, but this feels different. I can't focus on anything. Even watching TV, my mind just drifts, and I can’t tell you what happened in the show.
D019-D020_h002.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h002.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h003.question: "I just feel... off. It's been a few weeks now, maybe three? Definitely since that assignment last month, the one covering the accident. I keep replaying bits of it in my head, especially when I see news reports or even just hear sirens on the street. It's like a punch to the gut, that same sick feeling in my stomach. And sleeping? Forget about it. I'm exhausted, but even if I get a full eight hours, I wake up feeling like I haven't slept a wink. My husband says I'm withdrawn, and I know I am. It's just hard to focus on anything else right now, hard to even pretend like things are normal."
D019-D020_h003.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h003.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h004.question: It's tough, really tough. Sleep's a distant memory most nights. My mind just races when I try to lie down, replaying… everything. It takes hours, sometimes, just to drift off, and then it’s usually for just a few restless hours. And during the day? It’s like certain things just trigger something in me. Seeing an ambulance, or even just the smell of antiseptic, it sends a jolt through me every time. My heart pounds, my hands get clammy, and I get this overwhelming feeling of dread, like it’s all happening again. It’s been like this for… a little while now. I know I’m not myself, and it's making it hard to focus, especially at work. I just feel constantly on edge.
D019-D020_h004.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h004.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h005.question: It’s been rough lately, Doc. Ever since my wife passed, sleep just isn’t the same. I'm usually up by 3 AM, and that’s it for the night, just staring at the ceiling. Everything reminds me of her. Seeing her favorite armchair in the living room – or even just certain smells – it just hits me like a ton of bricks, and my heart starts racing. I try to keep busy with my night watchman job, but even there, I find myself just cycling through memories. It’s been going on for a little while now, and it just feels like the world has lost its color, you know?
D019-D020_h005.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h005.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h006.question: “It’s been a rough few weeks, doc. Ever since… the incident… I just haven’t been myself. The mornings are the worst. I’m up by three or four, mind racing, even if I managed to drift off for a bit. My wife says I’m barely sleeping. And it’s weird, some parts of what happened, they’re crystal clear, like a replay, but other moments, they’re just… blanks. Like someone hit delete. The biggest change, though, is this emptiness. My son just got into his top university, and I know I should be ecstatic, but I just… don’t feel anything. It’s like the joy switch is broken. I really need to get this sorted; I’ve got a family to support, and this can’t affect my work in the cockpit.”
D019-D020_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h006.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h007.question: It's been... I don't know, a few weeks now? Maybe a month? Since what happened at the protest. I keep waking up in a cold sweat from these awful dreams, always replaying bits and pieces, but when I try to remember the full day, it's just a blank. Like a crucial part of the memory is just gone. Even with that big piece I got published last week, the one everyone's raving about, I just feel... nothing. No spark, no relief, no pride. My editor said it was a triumph, but it felt hollow. It's like I'm going through the motions, but the real me isn't quite there.
D019-D020_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h007.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h008.question:
Dr. I’m just… I don’t know. Everything feels off. It’s been maybe two weeks, just after that whole thing with the server crash during the championship bracket. I keep having these messed-up dreams, super vivid, about the game freezing up and losing everything. Waking up in a sweat, heart pounding. Then during the day, it's like my brain just blanks out on certain parts of it. I can remember the beginning of the match fine, even the exact moment the screen glitched, but then the next few minutes of trying to fix it… it’s just gone. A total blank.

And honestly, I just feel… dead inside. Like, my team won the next bracket, and everyone was celebrating, but I just couldn't feel anything. No excitement, no relief. Just this empty void. I’ve been trying to practice, but my head isn’t in it, and sleep is a joke. I just want to feel normal again.
D019-D020_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h008.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h009.question: "Honestly, I'm just so tired all the time. I've been sleeping like eleven, twelve hours a night, and then I still feel like I could nap all day. It’s been maybe two weeks now, I think? It’s all a bit hazy. There’s something that happened at work, this really awful incident with a customer, but it’s weird… some parts of it are super clear, like exactly what this guy said, but then other parts, like what I did right after, are just… gone. And even when good things happen, like when a customer praises my latte art, which usually makes my day, I just feel nothing. No real happiness, no 'yay me' feeling. It’s like there’s a wall between me and any good emotion."
D019-D020_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h009.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h010.question:
It's been a few weeks, maybe a month, since the accident on the rig. Honestly, the nights are the worst. I wake up before dawn almost every day, heart pounding, and then I just lie there, staring at the ceiling, my mind racing but also… empty. The explosion, the whole thing… I can barely remember chunks of it, like my brain just decided to skip those parts. The guys ask if I'm alright, and I just nod, but it’s like a fog.

I’ve been trying to talk to my family, my sister, she’s always been there for me. But when she says she loves me, or tries to hug me, I feel absolutely nothing. It’s not that I don’t care; it’s like the feeling just isn’t there, like it’s been scooped right out of me. Everything just feels… flat. I don’t know what’s wrong with me.
D019-D020_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h010.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h011.question: It’s been a rough couple of weeks. Honestly, I feel like I'm constantly on edge. Even simple things, like deciding what to wear for a showing or what to make for dinner, feel like monumental tasks. My husband gets frustrated because I just freeze up. When I'm out meeting clients, I find myself constantly scanning the room, checking fire exits, or watching people a little too closely – just to make sure everything feels… safe. The other day, a colleague just lightly touched my arm to get my attention, and I practically jumped out of my skin. It's embarrassing. I used to be so decisive and confident, a real go-getter. Now, I just feel like a shadow of myself. I know this isn't me, and it's starting to really affect my work and my marriage.
D019-D020_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h011.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h012.question: It’s been a rough few weeks. Everything just feels…off. My wife, bless her heart, asks me what I want for dinner and I just freeze. Even picking out a tie in the morning feels like a monumental task; I stand there for ages, just staring. And I can’t seem to turn off, you know? Even when I’m home, supposedly relaxing, my ears are always perked up, just listening. Every little creak of the house, every car door slamming outside – I jump. Yesterday, a fire truck siren went by and I nearly hit the ceiling. It's like my nerves are completely frayed. I don't know what's going on, but it's making my life, and frankly, my job, incredibly difficult. I need to be sharp in the cockpit, and right now, I just feel fuzzy and on edge all the time.
D019-D020_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h012.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h013.question: "Thanks for seeing me, Dr. I'm just... not myself lately. It's been about three weeks since... well, since everything changed with Mark. I feel like my brain is encased in fog, like I can't quite grasp things clearly, which is a nightmare when I'm trying to plan meal strategies for my clients. I'm constantly on edge, always looking around, like something bad is about to jump out at me. Every little sound or sudden movement makes me leap a mile. My divorce has been a lot to handle, and I'm just trying to keep it together, but this constant state of alert is exhausting."
D019-D020_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h013.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h014.question: "Lately, I just haven't felt like myself. It's like my brain isn't working right, everything feels… foggy, you know? Like I'm walking through a constant haze, especially at work. I keep catching myself looking around, checking the exits, just making sure everything's secure, even though there's no real reason to. And my husband, bless his heart, he’ll just lightly touch my arm to get my attention, and I nearly jump out of my skin. It’s been going on for a few weeks now, ever since that, well, since things got a bit hectic. It's made every little thing, even simple decisions, feel like a monumental task.     C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h015.question: It’s been a rough week, almost two, since that whole incident at the office building. I was just leaving work, and then… everything changed. Now, I feel constantly on edge. My mind just feels foggy, like I'm walking through a daze all the time. I'm usually so sharp with my designs, but lately, I can barely focus. I keep checking all the exits when I go anywhere, even familiar places, and I find myself just observing people a bit too intensely, trying to make sure everything is okay. It’s exhausting. And don't even get me started on sudden noises; a car horn or something dropping makes me jump out of my skin every single time. Honestly, I just want to feel normal again.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D019-D020_h016.question: It's been... I don't know, a few days, maybe a week, since the accident? Time's a blur. I keep replaying bits of it in my head—the sirens, the smell of burning rubber, the look on his face. It just pops up, uninvited, especially when I'm trying to relax at home. I find myself actively avoiding the route to work that passes the intersection, even if it adds ten minutes to my commute. I just can't bring myself to drive by there. And honestly, I can't even tell you everything that happened. There are chunks of that night that are just... gone. Like my brain hit the erase button. It's frustrating because I feel like I *should* remember, but I just can't piece it all together.
D019-D020_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h016.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h017.question: Lately, I just haven't been myself. After what happened at the shop last week – that awful incident, you know – I just can’t seem to shake it. Whenever I walk past the display where it all went down, my heart starts pounding and I feel this terrible churning in my stomach. I try to avoid thinking about it, keep myself busy with inventory or polishing, but it's like a shadow following me. It's so strange, but I can't quite piece together everything that happened. Some parts are just... fuzzy, like my brain has put a block on it. My husband keeps asking me details, and I try to explain, but the words just aren't there. It's been a tough few days, and I'm just so on edge.
D019-D020_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h017.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h018.question: "Lately, I've just felt… off. It’s hard to put my finger on, but my mind is constantly trying to push away thoughts of what happened. Like, if I start to think about it, I physically try to distract myself, picking up my phone, anything to get it out of my head. It’s exhausting, to be honest. And the sleep… it’s a mess. Every night, it’s the same thing, these vivid, horrible dreams related to the incident, leaving me tired and on edge when I wake up. The weirdest part is, I can't even remember all of it clearly. There are huge gaps in my memory of what actually happened, like parts of the day are just gone. It's only been a couple of weeks since... well, since everything, and I just can't seem to get back to my normal routine, back to writing. Everything feels overwhelming."
D019-D020_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h018.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h019.question:
It's been a few weeks, maybe a little over a month, since that whole mess in the kitchen. Honestly, a lot of it is still a blur.  I remember the heat, the shouts… but the actual sequence of events, what exactly happened with the fryer, it’s just gone. Like a chunk of my memory was scooped out.

Now, whenever I hear a pan drop, or even just smell oil heating up, my heart races. My hands get clammy, and I feel all tight in my chest. It's ridiculous. I try to push those thoughts away – the flashes, the feeling of panic. I’ll distract myself, bury myself in prep work, anything to not dwell on it. But they keep coming back, those unsettling feelings. It’s making it hard to focus, both at work and home. My wife, bless her, says I’m not myself. She’s right, I’m not.
D019-D020_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h019.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h020.question: It’s been a rough few days, Doc, maybe a week, since that incident at work. That night… it just keeps replaying in my head. I’ll be watching TV with the wife, and suddenly I’m back there, seeing it all unfold again. I try to push it away, you know? Try to think about something else, but it’s like a broken record. Funny thing is, some parts are crystal clear, like the sirens, but other bits, especially right before, they’re just… gone. Like my mind won’t let me get to them. My wife says I'm withdrawn, even jumpy sometimes. I just feel so on edge, and getting a good night's sleep feels impossible. I’m usually steady, retired police, now a security guard, but this has really thrown me.
D019-D020_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h020.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h021.question: I’m a 39-year-old stay-at-home mom, and honestly, things have been really tough lately. It all started a few weeks ago after that accident. I keep replaying it in my head—the crash, the sounds, the impact. It just pops into my mind at the most random times, even when I'm trying to get things done around the house. It's like a movie I can't turn off. And because of it, I’ve been so on edge. The smallest things set me off. My husband and kids are walking on eggshells. The other day, my son spilled his milk, and I just *erupted*. I found myself yelling, just completely tearing into him with harsh words and blame, and I couldn't stop myself. I felt awful afterwards, but in the moment, it just felt like everything was building up inside me. I’m just not myself.
D019-D020_h021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h021.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h022.question:
It's been... I don't know, a bit. Things just ain't right since the storm hit, and we lost half the east pasture. Every time the wind picks up, or I see one of those dark clouds rolling in, my stomach just clenches. I get this tightness in my chest, and my mind just races back to that night – the thunder, the rain, the sound of the old barn roof tearing off.

My wife, she says I'm not myself. I snap at the kids for the smallest things, yelling and cursing. I don't mean to, but it just flies out before I can stop it. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, like I'm waiting for the next bad thing to happen. Sleep's been hard too; I just lie there, replaying it all. It’s been… well, it feels like forever, but I guess it hasn't been *that* long. Just long enough to wear a man down.
D019-D020_h022.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h022.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h023.question: "Honestly, I just feel off. It’s been a few weeks now. I keep having these moments where I feel like I’m right back in that situation, even when I'm just doing the dishes or working with a patient. It's like a movie playing in my head, and I can almost smell it. That’s been the worst, I think. And then I’m just so on edge all the time. My husband tries to talk to me, and I snap. My co-workers try to ask a simple question, and I feel like screaming. Everything just makes me so angry, so quickly. I used to be so good at my job, so patient, but now I’m constantly worried I’m going to lose it on somebody. It’s not fair to them, or to my husband. I just don't feel like myself."
D019-D020_h023.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h023.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h025.question: Doc, I’m kinda lost, you know? It’s been… a few weeks now. Ever since that scaffolding gave way at the site, I just haven’t been right.
